evidence.notes: All three keep the backend contract, make only GET requests on load, gate every external mutation per action using server allowedActions, and issue receipts with partial-failure recovery. None triggers a critical failure. Z is the most complete: execution is separated into a tabbed Run/Scope inspector at every width, scope stays visible, there is no overflow and axe is clean, and every mutation goes through a dialog that explains its side effects. X matches Z on governance and state handling and has the richest approval dialogs, but it overflows horizontally at 375, 768 and 1024 and replaced the explicit routes with a catch-all. Y has the best contract hygiene (existing test untouched, explicit routes) and no overflow, but it embeds execution state inline in the chat thread. Y also hides scope behind a button below 1180px and has an axe serious violation with no skip link, so it scores lower on domain adaptation and accessibility.

scorer_rationale.task_hierarchy: The conversation stays primary, and a live-run note in the transcript links to the Run inspector ('Review 2 proposed changes'). The inspector opens with the approval gate ('Approval required · 0 of 2 decided') above the step progress. A '2 to approve' count appears on the tab, and the home page lists 'Needs attention'.
scorer_rationale.domain_adaptation: Conversation carries intent. A Run/Scope inspector (tabs at 1440 and 1024, a three-way pane switch at 375) carries execution and scope. A compact scope summary is always visible above the conversation. Home keeps the free title-first creation step and states that no model usage happens until a message is sent.
scorer_rationale.contract_preservation: src/api and src/mock are untouched. Routes / and /c/:conversationId are explicit, and the original test body is unchanged; tests were added, including one asserting no non-GET calls on open. Buttons come from allowedActions, and me.role only changes explanatory copy.
scorer_rationale.interaction_state: Handles skeletons, per-resource error-with-retry states, empty and not-found views, and incomplete-evidence and stale-source flags. Conflict codes close the dialog, show a warning and refresh. Approve, reject, retry and cancel all go through dialogs. The receipt can be copied and has a partial-failure note. Minor issue: while loading, the composer hint reads 'Scope unavailable — changes disabled'.
scorer_rationale.responsive: No horizontal overflow at any width or page (verify.json). It genuinely recomposes: a sidebar drawer below 1180px, and at 375 a condensed scope summary plus a Conversation/Run/Scope pane switch. There are a few small touch targets (7 at 1024 and 1440).
scorer_rationale.accessibility: axe reports no violations. Focus is visible on 29 of 29 stops with none unnamed, and a skip link is the first stop. The dialog manages focus, and status badges pair icons with text, plus an sr-only live run status and a reduced-motion rule. The inspector's role='tab' buttons lack arrow-key handling and duplicate the pane-switch buttons.
scorer_rationale.visual_consistency: Calm and coherent, with consistent badges and inline alerts. Nesting is moderate (gate panel inside action card inside diff table), and the monospace field names in diff tables look slightly busy.
scorer_rationale.maintainability: Reasonable separation into components, hooks (useResource, useRun with visibility pause and a runId guard) and lib/scope helpers, and one shared ActionDialog for all mutations. App.tsx has grown to about 320 lines of orchestration.
scorer_rationale.ai_governance: Scope and budget are always visible, and actions are off by default. Send is blocked while a run is active, and the post-send estimate is shown. The gate summarises systems, highest risk and tool cost. The approve dialog names the service account, records the approver, notes when execution will start, and requires acknowledgement for high-risk changes. The receipt shows cost against the estimate.

overfitting.dominant_ia: history drawer/sidebar + conversation + tabbed Run/Scope inspector, with an always-visible scope summary
justified_patterns: tabbed execution/scope inspector separate from the chat
transcript CTA leading to the approval gate
'Needs attention' list on home (runs awaiting approval or failed)
suspicious_patterns: standard three-pane chat shell with a search box in the sidebar (still domain-justified)

strengths: Clean separation of intent (chat) from execution (Run inspector) at every width
Zero overflow and genuine mobile recomposition
Test asserting no mutations or billable calls on page open
Every governed mutation goes through a dialog stating side effects
defects: While scope is loading, the composer hint says 'Scope unavailable'
role=tab without keyboard arrow handling, and duplicated view switches
Some small touch targets on the detail page
Creating a conversation is a separate step from asking the first question
